# Narration Guide

<!-- Generated by `npm run guide` from scenes.json. Edit the text in scenes.json, then run it again. -->

11 scenes, 250 words, about 96 s of speech, 170 s planned on screen. The contest limit is 180 s; this project warns above 175 s.

## How to change the words and record your own voice

1. Edit `narration` for a scene in `demo/scenes.json`. Spell hard words the way they sound ("I D" for ID).
2. Record that scene alone, 44.1 or 48 kHz, one take per file. Keep a half second of quiet at each end.
3. Save it as `demo/public/audio/<scene-id>.wav` (`.mp3`, `.m4a` and `.aac` also work). Use the id in the table below.
   Your file replaces the machine voice for that scene. Delete your file to go back to the placeholder.
4. Run `npm run sync` (the studio and render scripts do this for you). The scene length follows your recording.
5. `npm run studio` to preview. `npm run render` for the full video, or `npm run render:scene -- s04-reveal out/s04.mp4` for one scene.

Machine-voice stand-ins: `npm run vo:placeholder` (uses the macOS `say` command, voice and speed set by
`PHANTOMTRACE_VO_VOICE` and `PHANTOMTRACE_VO_RATE`). Add `-- --all` to redo every scene after editing text.
The stand-in voice is only for timing. Replace it with your own before you submit.

## Pace and length

- Plan on about 2.6 words per second. A scene with 26 words needs about 10 seconds.
- Each scene lasts as long as your recording plus 0.6 s, or its video clip if that is longer.
- If the total is too long, cut words first, then trim clips with `trimStartSec` in `scenes.json`.

### 1. The problem (`s01-problem`)

Voice file: `demo/public/audio/s01-problem.wav` · Plan: 12 s · 20 words (about 8 s read aloud)

> You try to eject a drive, and Finder says a program may be using it. It never says which one.

Screen: Optional live clip. In Finder, select PhantomDemo, press Cmd+E. Let the dialog sit for 3 seconds.

On-screen labels: "Finder names no program" at 3 s

### 2. The old way (`s02-old-way`)

Voice file: `demo/public/audio/s02-old-way.wav` · Plan: 12 s · 16 words (about 6 s read aloud)

> Today that means lsof, guesswork, and sometimes pulling the cable. Even diskutil names only one process.

Screen: Optional live clip instead of the replay: run both commands in Terminal against the demo drive.

On-screen labels: "Replayed from docs/CliCapture.md (real output)" at 1 s

### 3. The trigger (`s03-trigger`)

Voice file: `demo/public/audio/s03-trigger.wav` · Plan: 12 s · 16 words (about 6 s read aloud)

> PhantomTrace starts right where you are stuck. Right-click the volume, and choose Why Can't I Eject?

Screen: REQUIRED. Finder, right-click PhantomDemo on the Desktop or sidebar, Quick Actions, Why Can't I Eject? Stop when the PhantomTrace window opens. About 10 seconds.

Record with: `Scripts/demo/record-clip.sh s03-trigger 12` (saves `demo/public/clips/s03-trigger.mp4`).

On-screen labels: "Finder Quick Action" at 2 s

Voice file: `demo/public/audio/s04-reveal.wav` · Plan: 20 s · 35 words (about 13 s read aloud)

Screen: Optional live clip. Let the window open, then slowly move the pointer over each row.

Voice file: `demo/public/audio/s06-egress.wav` · Plan: 18 s · 22 words (about 8 s read aloud)

## Honest-claims check

Say only what the video shows. The Kiro scene says hooks "check" things before commits, because the hook
output was not captured (see `docs/KiroUsage.md`). If you add a claim, add its proof to the repo first.
